newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London steady, awaiting data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London steady, awaiting data.

text.p: U.S. stocks trading in London were steady to marginally higher in quiet trade on Monday as investors awaited key economic data from the U.S. and remained wary ahead of the FOMC meeting later this week.

Traders said economic figures due at 1230 GMT in the U.S. were likely to set the tone for the Dow's opening. Personal income and spending data will be followed at 1400 GMT by new home sales and the Chicago purchasing managers survey.
On Friday U.S. stocks ended with modest gains but over the five-day period, the Dow had lost 109 points.
Investors were likely to remain cautious until after the FOMC meeting on July 1/2, though few analysts expected the Fed to raise short term interest rates this time around.
Among active shares in London AT&T was down $1/4 at $35-1/2 after the Wall Street Journal said the chairman of SBC Communications had called off merger talks with the telecoms giant.
Shares in General Electric were $3/16 lower at $65-1/8 on the back of negative comments in Barron's financial weekly, traders said.
Elsewhere, Gillette was off $1/4 at $95-7/8, General Motors climbed $3/16 to $56 and Intel rose $1/4 to $142-1/2.
"The rest of the market has been very quiet," one trader said. "Most stocks are steady to a fraction better and we're waiting for the data later today."
